rounds.text: Trigyn Technologies Ltd trades at a price-to-book ratio of just 0.79x based on a price of ₹ 53.5 against a book value of ₹ 67.4 [E2], and key-ratios data shows an even more discounted P/B of 0.22x compared to a sector benchmark of 2.07x [E7]. The company's valuation metrics are compellingly low, featuring a P/E ratio of 17.09x against a sector benchmark of 22.3x [E6]. Operating margins have demonstrated a substantial structural turnaround, expanding by 14 percentage points from negative 8 percent three years earlier to 6 percent in March 2026 [E30]. Over a five-year horizon, fundamentals have significantly outpaced the stock performance, with profit growing by 15 percent while the price declined by 18 percent, generating a fundamentals-led signal of potential undervaluation [E57]. A discounted cash flow model puts intrinsic value at ₹ 64 per share, offering a 16.2 percent margin of safety above the current market price of ₹ 53.5 [E46, E47], while a reverse DCF indicates that the market price only requires 12.6 percent earnings growth compared to the 15.0 percent assumed in the base case [E48]. Conceded: [E4], [E31], [E73].

The bull points to a P/B of 0.79x and a discounted P/B of 0.22x against the sector [E2, E7], but this cheapness is misleading when the company generates a return on assets of just 1.03% while the sector benchmark achieves 4.77% [E8]. The argument that operating margins improved over a three-year period [E30] completely ignores the more urgent reality that quarterly operating margin contracted by 5 percentage points to 6% in March 2026 compared to the year-ago period [E31]. The reliance on a DCF model to claim intrinsic value [E46] overlooks the explicit screen warning that the rationale for bearish concern is precisely that it trades below DCF value [E73], reflecting hidden risks the models fail to capture. Furthermore, the bull emphasizes a 15% profit growth over five years [E57], yet the stock sits only 25% up its 52-week range [E5] and returns a dividend yield of exactly 0.00% [E4], meaning shareholders receive zero cash return while waiting for the fundamentals to materialize. Conceded: [E1], [E6], [E48].
